title: observability: add token-level KV cache metrics, dashboards and tuned alerts
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Added token-level KV cache metrics and dashboards; tuned alerts to reduce noise. No breaking API changes.
description:
Motivation: we need finer-grained observability into the KV cache and per-token cost/latency so SRE and platform teams can diagnose regressions in latency and identify cost hot spots. This PR instruments token-level KV metrics (hits/misses/evictions), per-token latency breakdowns, and integrates those metrics into Datadog dashboards with tuned alerts to reduce false positives.

What this PR does: - Adds runtime instrumentation for KV cache events (kv.cache.token_hit, kv.cache.token_miss, kv.cache.token_eviction) with labels: model, deployment, route, customer_tier, sequence_length_bucket. - Emits per-token latency and cost breakdowns (token.latency_ms, token.cost_usd) keyed by the same labels and request_id for correlation. - Adds a new Datadog dashboard template (Observability / Token-level KV & Cost) with views for: overall KV hit ratio, hit ratio by model/deployment, token latency P50/P95/P99 by sequence length bucket, per-route cost per 1k tokens, and correlation panels (KV hit vs tail latency). - Introduces a lightweight sampling mode for high-volume customers to limit cardinality while preserving representative histograms (config flag: observability.kv_token_sampling_rate, default 1.0). - Adds alert tuning: replaces a previously noisy tail-latency alert with a composite alert that combines token-level KV hit-rate drops with sustained P99 token latency > 250ms for 5 minutes. - Updates runbooks and adds a short playbook for incident owners describing how to use the new dashboard panels to triage KV-related regressions.

Backward compatibility & rollout: instrumentation is additive and guarded behind a feature flag (obs.token_kv_metrics_enabled). Default is enabled for internal and dedicated fleets; rollout to hosted tenants will be gradual and observable. Sampling mode prevents explosion of cardinality for large tenants.

Checklist: - [x] Runtime metrics and labels implemented - [x] Datadog dashboard JSON and template added - [x] Alert definitions and runbook updated - [x] Unit tests for metric emission - [x] E2E smoke test against staging datadog endpoint - [x] Documentation snippet added to observability docs

Notes: metric names follow our existing naming conventions and include unit metadata. We've validated disk/network overhead in internal load tests and observed ~0.5% CPU increase at tail-heavy workloads with sampling_rate=1.0 and ~0.1% with sampling_rate=0.1.
commits: feat(runtime): emit token-level KV cache metrics with model/deployment/route labels
feat(obs): add token-level latency and cost metrics, include request_id for correlation
chore(dashboards): add Datadog dashboard JSON and template for token-KV and cost breakdowns
perf(obs): add sampling mode to limit metric cardinality (config: observability.kv_token_sampling_rate)
docs(runbook): update observability runbook and incident triage steps
changed_files: runtime/service/kv_metrics.go -- added KV event instrumentation and label extraction
runtime/service/metrics_test.go -- unit tests for metric emission
observability/alerts/token_kv_alerts.yaml -- composite alert rules and thresholds
docs/observability.md -- added section describing token-level metrics and dashboard usage
telemetry/publishers/datadog_publisher.go -- map new metrics to datadog tags and histogram units
review_comments: Diego Morales: Overall this looks good. Two requests: (1) Add a per-tenant sampling override and (2) make the sequence_length_bucket boundaries configurable. Can you address?
Author (Aisha Patel): Added per-tenant override via config store (config/tenant_overrides) and made sequence length buckets configurable; updated docs to reflect default bucket values.

Priya Singh: The alert threshold for composite alert looks reasonable, but I'm concerned about the 5 minute window being too short for scheduled GC spikes. Can we add an adaptive suppression during scheduled maintenance windows?
Author (Aisha Patel): Added an optional alert_suppression_windows config and patched the alert rule to ignore maintenance window metadata. Also added guidance to the runbook.
Evan Zhang: Unit tests look good. One nit: prefer constants for metric names in telemetry package to avoid typos across publishers.
Author (Aisha Patel): Refactored metric name constants into telemetry/metrics_names.go and updated publishers and runtime to import the constants.
ci_checks: CI: integration (staging datadog) — flaky on first run (timeout), rerun passed
notes_on_rollout: Rollout plan: 1) Deploy to internal fleets, monitor KV hit-rate and token-latency dashboards for 24h; 2) Enable on dedicated customers with opt-in via admin console for 48h; 3) Gradual hosted tenant rollout in 10% increments with sampling_rate=0.1; 4) Increase sampling_rate as needed. Observability alerts initially set to notify #sre-observability and #platform-ops with low-severity tagging.
post_merge_tasks: Monitor the new dashboard for two weeks and iterate thresholds
Add Grafana/Prometheus compatibility layer for on-prem deployments (follow-up PR)
Coordinate with Pricing team to record any observed billing changes due to metric emissions
changelog_summary: Add token-level KV cache metrics, dashboards, sampling controls, and tuned composite alerts to reduce noise and enable faster KV-related triage.
